:::{#exm-counting-measure}
#### Counting measure on the non-negative integers

For the counting measure $\mu$ on $\set{0, 1, 2, \ldots}$,
$\mu(\set{0, 1, 2}) = 3$,
and the set of even numbers has $\mu(\set{0, 2, 4, \ldots}) = \infty$.
The even numbers are the union of the pairwise disjoint sets
$\set{0}, \set{2}, \set{4}, \ldots$,
and countable additivity agrees:
$\sum_{k=0}^{\infty} \mu(\set{2k}) = 1 + 1 + \cdots = \infty$.

:::

{{< slidebreak >}}

:::{#rem-measure-size}
#### Measures generalize size

A [measure](#def-measure) generalizes size:
it can measure how many elements a set has,
as in @def-counting-measure,
or how long a set of real numbers is,
as [Lebesgue measure](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lebesgue_measure) does,
assigning each interval $[a, b]$ its length $b - a$.
For example, the counting measure of $\set{2, 3, 4, 5}$ is $4$,
while the Lebesgue measure of the interval $[2, 5]$ is $5 - 2 = 3$.
Both appear as reference measures in the
[Fubini--Tonelli theorem](calculus.qmd#thm-fubini-tonelli).

:::
